provenance.seriesName: Q21 — Neighbors: Immigrants/foreign workers (would not like)
provenance.note: SOURCE SWITCHED 2026-08-27 from Gallup's Migrant Acceptance Index to World Values Survey Wave 7, Q21. Gallup covered 8 of 9 peers in 2016/17 and only 4 of 9 in 2019 (and precisely the 4 highest scorers), which is why this gauge sat unscored; WVS Wave 7 is the only source confirmed to cover all 9. Every value is the WVS Online Analysis tool's own "Show Column % (excluding DK/NA)" figure — the share of valid answers who would not like immigrants/foreign workers as neighbours — read directly from the provider's own screen, not computed here. The valid base is used deliberately: the tool's default "% of Total" view puts don't-knows and refusals in the denominator, and DK/NA rates range from 0% to 6.2% across these nine, which makes that view systematically non-comparable. Each country contributes its own fieldwork year (2017-2022), scored on the latest-wave-per-country basis. Valid N per country: AUS 1,813 (2018), CAN 4,018 (2020), GBR 2,585 (2022), NZL 1,057 (2020), KOR 1,245 (2018), NLD 2,057 (2022), USA 2,436 (2017), DEU 1,523 (2018), JPN 1,311 (2019). PERCENTAGES ARE WEIGHTED. WVS documents this nowhere; it was established by inference from the tool's own arithmetic — see METHODOLOGY.md's "Are the Online Analysis percentages weighted?" for the evidence and the residual. Great Britain only: WVS fields Northern Ireland as a separate study (9.5%, N=446), and combining the two would be computing rather than republishing. The exclusion cannot move Australia's score — Germany and Japan set the min-max bounds, not Great Britain.
